question: Does restricting original native recorded site×species positives to the complete acoustic+visual method pair change the descriptive site-level prevalence/richness contrasts among intervention, control and artificial wetland categories?

source.study: Wenner et al. (2025), Global Ecology and Conservation 62 e03837; data Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15044115 CC BY 4.0

fixed_design.analysis_cohort: Published Q1: 27 sites; exclude kis-banyato and vadasz-turjan; 13 intervention, 6 control, 8 artificial.
fixed_design.analysis_grain: site×species presence as OR of recorded native count>0 across actual rows/dates/methods, all or acoustic+visual only.
fixed_design.site_richness: number of original nine species with observed source-positive at each site (full/core separately)
fixed_design.model: no occupancy, GLM or p-values; simple descriptive proportions at fixed source sites

fixed_outputs: for each category: sites, native source-positive site×species, retained in AV, omitted in AV, mean observed recorded site richness full/core
for 9 taxa × 3 categories: number of source-positive sites full and AV, original native recording fraction, core-only fraction and loss
for each species × category contrast: raw/native prevalence difference versus AV core difference, shifts in percentage points, strict non-zero sign reversals, contrasts involving ties separately
for each group: distinct site×date groups with dipnet/bottletrap source method rows represented, not deployment/effort
for 27 original sites: site-level full and AV source-recorded richness values with category and loss
source count, source classification/labels, no creation of positives and exact all-method 144 vs paired-core 104 row source check
proof_boundaries: Comparison is within unchanged source sites and method records; reduction in positives is a deterministic method-record restriction, not a causal experimental effect.
Categories are original observational categories, not randomized treatment. No causal restoration effect or ecological difference inferred.
Source method-row missing is not equivalent to a field method not performed. Article reports dipnet use in standard visits whereas many archived dipnet rows are absent.
Cross-method detection and positive source record prevalence are not occupancy estimates, true absence, comparable detection probability or species richness corrected for sampling effort.
No new A/B/M, field sampling closure, ecological world count, original unmarked fitted coefficient or EOG-WF fourth scored endpoint.
